=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:838-839 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: If saving immediate state fails after a successful POST, the reservation remains pending and its report-cap slot is consumed, while the target is not recorded in immediate-state.json.
  WHY: The reviewer reports no runtime misbehavior or duplicate report; the pattern is still filed, but the exact target cannot be looked up from immediate-state.json.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:503-514 | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The _filing_lock context manager does not provide mutual exclusion between separate processes opening filing.lock independently.
  WHY: The reviewer states that on Linux each process receives a separate open file description, allowing concurrent read-modify-write operations on immediate-state.json and filed-state.json to corrupt or lose reported-signature state.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

The PR docs describe behavior that relies on the fixed code, but production code in .claude/ does not implement that behavior.

- requirement: "The hook passes the SHA-256 of the line it logged, so the report is about that prompt even when another one is logged first." (PR description, CLAUDE.md §23.I)
  expected_change_site: .claude/hooks/permission_prompt_logger.py spawn_reporter and main
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  EVIDENCE: The .claude/hooks/permission_prompt_logger.py spawn_reporter function (lines 98-109 in the PR diff) accepts no digest parameter and passes no --record-sha256 flag. The main() function (line 121) calls spawn_reporter(path, record["cwd"]) without computing or passing a digest. The twin copy workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/permission_prompt_logger.py includes both the digest parameter and record_digest(record) call, but the production .claude/ copy does not.
- requirement: "Each signature is reported once per session and at most 5 per session (kept per session id, so sessions sharing a home directory never suppress each other)" (PR description)
  expected_change_site: .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py _load_immediate_state, _report_now, _file_pending
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  EVIDENCE: The .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py _load_immediate_state (lines 517-525 in the PR diff) returns the flat structure {"reports": {sig: ...}, "count": n} keyed by signature only, with no session isolation. The _report_now function (lines 728-770) uses immediate["reports"] and immediate["count"] without per-session bucketing. The _file_pending function (lines 626-635) checks sig in reported without session filtering.
- requirement: "The signature is reserved (pending) before the POST, so no local write failure can make report-now post it twice" (PR description, AD-10)
  expected_change_site: .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py _report_now
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  EVIDENCE: The .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py _report_now (lines 759-770 in the PR diff) posts to GitHub first (line 760), then saves state (lines 765-769). The reserve-before-POST pattern with PENDING_TARGET, _release_reservation, and the try/except around the POST exists only in the twin copy. The .claude/ copy does not define PENDING_TARGET and does not reserve before posting.

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:503-514 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The _filing_lock context manager uses fcntl.flock() on file descriptors independently opened by each process, which does not provide mutual exclusion between separate processes.
  WHY: On Linux, flock() locks are associated with the open file description, not the inode. When the detached report-now process and the file process each independently open filing.lock via Path.open("a"), they each receive separate open file descriptions. Both processes can acquire their own independent exclusive lock on the file simultaneously. This allows concurrent read-modify-write operations on immediate-state.json and filed-state.json, leading to potential corruption or loss of reported signature state when two sessions attempt to file patterns or report prompts at the same time.
